implementation_notes: ADO.NET already ships the pattern: a DataTable is one table of in-memory relational data with Columns/Rows collections, constraints and row states, and a DataSet groups tables plus DataRelation objects - the closest literal implementation of Fowler's Record Set in a mainstream stack, and the natural container for Table Module logic. What replaces a hand-rolled row/column structure is this library type; the modern alternative when the shape is fixed is a typed record (record OrderRow(long Id, decimal Total)) materialised with a DbDataReader loop or an ORM projection. Keep DataTable for genuinely dynamic projections or direct grid binding, and strip its change-tracking payload (row state, schema) before shipping it across a boundary.
pitfalls: DataTable columns are object-typed: every read boxes and a type mismatch throws InvalidCastException at the read site; DataRow.Field<T> is the safe accessor, and a typed DataSet removes the problem entirely.
DataRow carries row state (Added/Modified/Deleted) and AcceptChanges semantics - editing rows in place turns the value into a change tracker, and its serialised form leaks schema and pending state.
Serialising a DataSet with XML keeps the whole schema (table and column names included), and ReadXml on untrusted input adds a deserialisation surface.
